document.title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content:
IS 5701 (Part 2):2025
CODE FOR BREEDING, CARE, MANAGEMENT AND HOUSING OF LABORATORY ANIMALS - PART 2 LABORATORY RABBITS
(Second Revision, February 2025)
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 1.1 This standard lays down guidelines for the breeding, care, management, and housing of laboratory rabbits.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 1.2 This standard is Part 2 of a ten-part laboratory-animal series under the Animal Husbandry and Equipment Sectional Committee, FAD 32, Food and Agriculture Division Council (ICS 65.020.30). Other parts in the series cover mice/rats, guinea pigs, hamsters, snakes, frogs, chicks, pigeons, mosquitoes, and other laboratory animals.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 2.1 Rabbits should be housed in stable, suitable groups when appropriate after weaning, with careful age and sex considerations.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 2.2 Environmental enrichment includes provision of hay/roughage, chewable items, retreat/burrow-like spaces, visual barriers, and exercise opportunities.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 2.3 The standard directly links environmental enrichment and exercise with normal skeletal and muscular development and overall animal welfare.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 3.1 Bedding provisions require dry, non-absorbent material placed in the nesting area, which must be stored in clean and dry conditions.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 3.2 Feeding provisions mandate pelleted feed, grass hay/greens, gradual food changes, and monitored water consumption.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 3.3 Feed-batch records, including manufacturing date and expiry information, are mandatory components of the feeding management provisions.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 4.1 Disease-control procedures, health monitoring, veterinary oversight, and facility-management requirements must be documented and maintained.
chunks.document_title: Code for Breeding, Care, Management and Housing of Laboratory Animals — Part 2 Laboratory Rabbits

chunks.content: 4.2 Breeding and reproductive biology provisions require humane care, with specific protocols for potentially painful or invasive procedures and humane endpoints in the animal welfare framework.
